name: Visual Node Script
description: A program you assemble instead of type, with wires that refuse to lie. Nodes have typed ports and a connection between mismatched types is rejected at the moment it is attempted rather than at run time — which is the entire pedagogical argument for visual scripting: the error arrives while the player is still thinking about the thing that caused it. Cycles are permitted only through nodes that declare themselves loop-safe, since an unguarded cycle is an infinite loop the player cannot see. The graph compiles to an instruction list rather than executing itself, which is what lets utility.sandboxed_vm impose limits that a self-executing graph could always escape.

inputs.name: nodeLibrary
inputs.description: Available node kinds with their typed ports. Required — the library is the language.

inputs.name: strictTypes
inputs.description: Whether mismatched wires are refused as they are drawn. Off makes errors arrive late, which is the thing this form exists to prevent.

inputs.name: allowCycles
inputs.description: Whether cycles are permitted outside loop-safe nodes.

inputs.name: maxNodes
inputs.description: Nodes a single program may contain.

outputs.name: compiled
outputs.description: Instruction list produced from the graph.

outputs.name: typeErrors
outputs.description: Rejected connections with the types that clashed.
